title: “Apply the history step” clears “reload pending” before both of its consumers read it

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

[Apply the history step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#apply-the-history-step) sets a document state’s [reload pending](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-reload-pending) to _false_, and then two separate consumers read that same flag afterwards. Both therefore always see _false_ — and both are unreachable as written.

> Set _targetEntry_’s [document state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#she-document-state)’s [reload pending](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-reload-pending) to false.
>
> Let _allowPOST_ be _targetEntry_’s [document state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#she-document-state)’s [reload pending](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-reload-pending).
>
> In parallel, [attempt to populate the history entry’s document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#attempt-to-populate-the-history-entry's-document) for _targetEntry_, given _navigable_, … **with _allowPOST_ set to _allowPOST_** and _completionSteps_ set to …

### Consumer 1: _allowPOST_

Read directly from the flag the previous step just cleared — so it’s unconditionally false. Its only use is in [attempt to populate the history entry’s document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#attempt-to-populate-the-history-entry's-document):

> Otherwise, if all of the following are true:
>
> - _entry_’s URL’s scheme is a [fetch scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-scheme); and
> - _documentResource_ is null, or **_allowPOST_ is true** and _documentResource_’s [request body](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#post-resource-request-body) is not failure
>
> then set _navigationParams_ to the result of [create navigation params by fetching](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#create-navigation-params-by-fetching) …

When the entry has a [POST resource](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#post-resource), _documentResource_ is non-null; so, with _allowPOST_ false, this condition can never hold — and _navigationParams_ is never set. Reloading a POST result can therefore never re-fetch. The ordinary [navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate) path passes _allowPOST_ set to _true_ explicitly; so, only the traversal/reload path is affected — which is exactly the path a reload takes.

### Consumer 2: The reload-navigation flag

[create navigation params by fetching](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#create-navigation-params-by-fetching) says:

> If _entry_’s [document state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#she-document-state)’s [reload pending](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-reload-pending) is true, then set _request_’s [reload-navigation flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-reload-navigation-flag).
>
> Otherwise, if _entry_’s [document state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#she-document-state)’s [ever populated](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-ever-populated) is true, then set _request_’s [history-navigation flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-history-navigation-flag).

That runs inside the populate above; i.e., strictly after the clear. So on a genuine reload, the reload-navigation flag is never set; and the `Otherwise` branch means the request is instead marked as a **_history_** navigation — which is the _opposite_ of what happened.

Both consequences follow from step ordering alone; no implementation race is involved. And two things suggest this is an ordering slip — rather than a deliberate design:

- First, earlier in the same algorithm, the spec asserts the flag is still live:

   > Switch on _navigationType_:
   >
   > “reload”
   > Assert: _targetEntry_’s [document state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#she-document-state)’s [reload pending](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-reload-pending) is true.

- Second, _allowPOST_ would be pointless as a parameter if the only caller that can pass a non-constant value always passes false.

### Implementations

No engine derives any of this from the flag; each engine keys reload behavior off its own load/nav type. So the ordering’s never been exercised:

- **Blink**:
  - `UpdateLoadFlagsWithCacheFlags` maps `NavigationType::RELOAD`→`net::LOAD_VALIDATE_CACHE` [`navigation_request.cc`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:content/browser/renderer_host/navigation_request.cc)
  - `FrameLoader::ResourceRequestForReload` uses `FetchCacheMode::kValidateCache` [`frame_loader.cc`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/frame_loader.cc)
- **Gecko**: `LOAD_RELOAD_NORMAL` maps to `nsIRequest::VALIDATE_ALWAYS` [`nsDocShellLoadState.cpp`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/docshell/base/nsDocShellLoadState.cpp)
- **WebKit**: `FrameLoader::reload` sets `ResourceRequestCachePolicy::ReloadIgnoringCacheData` [`FrameLoader.cpp`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/loader/FrameLoader.cpp)

Blink is also a good illustration of the distinction _allowPOST_ appears meant to draw — and which the current ordering erases. In that same switch, **reloading** a POST navigation re-fetches (`RELOAD`, plus a repost confirmation prompt) — while **traversing** to one is served from cache only (`RESTORE_WITH_POST` maps to `net::LOAD_ONLY_FROM_CACHE | net::LOAD_SKIP_CACHE_VALIDATION`).

Gecko draws the same distinction: Prompting via `nsDocShell::ConfirmRepost` before re-submitting on reload. Reload-vs-traverse is precisely what _allowPOST_ encodes — and per the spec text as currently written, it can’t currently encode it.

This surfaced in Ladybird as a user-visible bug: Reloading a page whose server had gone offline still rendered from cache — because the reload never revalidated: LadybirdBrowser/ladybird#10976. Implementing the reload-navigation-flag step strictly per the spec requirements as currently written produced dead code — for the reason above.

The Ladybird fix for that had to snapshot [reload pending](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-reload-pending) before the clear: https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/11004.

### Imaginable fixes

- Move the clear after the populate reading the flag + compute _allowPOST_ before it. Smallest change + makes both consumers live.
- Or pass the reload state into [attempt to populate the history entry’s document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#attempt-to-populate-the-history-entry's-document) explicitly — instead of having it re-read mutable state on the entry. So, the value can’t be invalidated between producer and consumer. That’d also removes the ordering hazard for the reload-navigation-flag step — which today reads the flag from a different algorithm entirely.
- Or, if reloading a POST resource is genuinely meant never to re-fetch, then say so — and drop _allowPOST_ from the traversal path. Right now the parameter reads as if it does something there when it actually in fact can’t.

Separately: It may be worth saying whether the reload-navigation flag is expected to affect caching at all. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-reload-navigation-flag) marks it _“for exclusive use by HTML’s [navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate) algorithm”_ — and **nothing** keys cache revalidation off it. So, an implementation following both specs literally has **_nothing_** that makes a reload revalidate (which is how this spec problem was found). See https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1899.
